events.description:
The normalized tool events the skill took producing this turn (assistant
turns only, and only when the harness exposed a tool transcript). Empty
otherwise. Surfaced for post-hoc analysis, streamed live, and rendered
into the transcript the judge sees.

Message.description: A single turn in the conversation.

oneOf.description: The (real or simulated) user driving the skill.
The skill / assistant under test.
System-level framing, if a provider surfaces it.

kind.description: `tool_call` (the skill invoked a tool) or `tool_result` (the observation).

name.description:
Normalized tool name where knowable (e.g. `bash`, `edit_file`); `None` for
a `tool_result` or when the harness did not name it.

input.description: Structured tool arguments (the command, the file path); `None` when none.

output.description: The result/observation text, when the transcript exposed it.

index.description: Position within the run, so ordering ("did X before Y") is expressible.

tool_call_id.description:
The harness's own stable identity for this call, joining a `tool_call` to
its `tool_result`. `None` means the harness exposed no identity — never an
empty string, which would read as an id that happens to be blank.

ToolEvent.description:
One normalized tool-call / action event the skill took during a turn, lifted
from `oneharness`'s `events` array (its `--events` output). Harness-agnostic,
so a consumer can inspect shell commands, file edits, and tool uses across any
harness, not just the final text. `input` is the structured, tool-shaped args
so a consumer can match on the command string or file path without re-parsing.

`input` is free-form JSON, so `Message`/`Transcript` are `PartialEq` but not
`Eq`.

op.description: The operation this frame asks for.

notes.description:
Every note delivered into this run so far (protocol v5). Omitted when
none has been, so a v4 double sees a byte-identical request.

schema.description: `supervisor`: decide completion, or produce the next user turn.
schema.title: SupervisorFrame

delivered_to.description:
The party that was handed it — **not** the same thing as its addressee: a
note is delivered to whoever is live, and the addressee is what the
recipient is told the note is *for*.

DeliveredNote.description: One note as it was handed to a party, with the party it reached.

Note.description:
One note: what the worker reads, who it is for, and the property it binds.

Built through [`Note::new`] / [`Note::to`] / [`Note::binding`] and in no other
way — `non_exhaustive` closes the struct literal, and deserialization goes
through the same conversion — so a note whose text nobody can read, or whose
criterion is unusable, is unrepresentable rather than representable and refused
somewhere later.

oneOf.description: An update to the *worker's* task.
An update to the *supervisor's* brief.
Addressed to both parties.

Addressee.description:
Who a note is for.

Required; there is no default, because a note whose addressee is guessed is a
note the judge may read as an instruction to itself. One run saw a simulated
user compose a four-point "manager ruling" in-conversation and instruct the
worker to post it over the run channel, and the worker complied.

Criterion.description:
The property a bound note requires of the finished work.

A validated newtype, checked in the conversion that builds it, so a [`Note`]
carrying an unusable criterion is unrepresentable rather than
representable-and-refused-somewhere-later. The rules are the ones an
orchestrator already enforces on authored plan criteria
(`orchestrator/criteria_guard.py` in `nickderobertis/ai-orchestrator`), ported
here so the *seam that accepts the note* refuses at the moment of binding
rather than at render time — after the turn has been composed — or by the
judge, which has already lost.

What the rules cannot catch, stated plainly: "this is a mechanism the author
preferred rather than a property the node owes" needs the author's intent, and
no pattern has it. What stands in for it is the rendered framing
([`Criteria::rendered`]), which instructs the judge to evaluate the property a
named mechanism was serving.

oneOf.description: The agent under test.
The simulated user / completion supervisor.

Party.description: Which party of the conversation a delivery reached.

oneOf.description: The invocation carried no classified failure, including an empty reply.

cause.description: The invocation's failure-kind token, candidate status, or error kind.

harness.description: The candidate that ran, or the last candidate attempted.

oneOf.description: The invocation carried a classified failure.

TurnOutcome.description: The classified outcome of the worker turn a supervisor is deciding.
